scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: rows that share one list
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We build a three by three grid of zeros, and set the top left cell to one. But three cells changed, one in every row. Multiplying a list repeats the same inner list three times. All three rows are one list. Build each row separately in a loop, and each row gets its own list.

props.fixedCode:
grid = []
for row in range(3):
    grid.append([0] * 3)
grid[0][0] = 1
print(grid)
props.why: Multiplying a list of lists repeats the same inner list three times, so all rows are one object; build each row separately.

shorts.title: A list of lists
shorts.hook: "A two dimensional list is a list whose items are lists."
shorts.script: A two dimensional list is a list whose items are lists. Each inner list is a row. Board equals bracket, bracket one, two, three, close, comma, bracket four, five, six, close, close. Two rows, three columns. Use it for tables, boards, seating charts, or anything laid out in rows and columns. Python has no special grid type, only lists inside lists. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: A grid of values.

shorts.title: Row, then column
shorts.hook: "To pick one cell of a grid, use two indexes."
shorts.script: To pick one cell of a grid, use two indexes. Board, bracket one, bracket two. The first bracket picks the row. The second picks the item inside that row. Row one, column two, gives six. Say row first, column second, every time, until it feels natural. You can assign to a cell too, and only that one number changes. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Two brackets, one cell.

shorts.title: Loop over a grid
shorts.hook: "To visit every cell, use two loops."
shorts.script: To visit every cell, use two loops. The outer loop walks over the rows. The inner loop walks over the cells in that row. Add each cell to a total, and you get the sum of the whole grid. This is the accumulator pattern, inside a nested loop. The same shape works for printing, searching, and counting cells. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Rows, then cells.

shorts.title: Rows that share
shorts.script: Here is a famous trap. You build a grid with bracket zero times three, close bracket, times three. You set one cell to one, and three cells change. The multiply repeated the same row three times. All the rows are one list. Build each row in a loop instead, and every row is its own separate list. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Build rows separately.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the two D list never get lost?"
shorts.script: Why did the two D list never get lost? It always knew its row and column. Your challenge. Build a three by three grid of zeros, using a loop. Make the middle cell equal to five. Then print the whole grid. Remember the middle is row one, column one, because we count from zero. Share your grid in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 31.
